confirmed_properties: A successful TerminateJobObject request suppresses a redundant TerminateProcess request against the same root.
For every retained root process HANDLE, the bounded WaitForSingleObject path runs in a separate try even when job or fallback per-process termination requests raise.
Root exit-code retrieval remains after the signaled-handle wait. Root/thread handle closing remains after the bounded wait attempt; job drainage and final job close remain unchanged.
Request/wait/close/drain errors are accumulated and remain fatal cleanup failures. Successful job termination is not treated as proof of completion.

primary_sources.supports: External termination is asynchronous; completion requires waiting on the process HANDLE. Repeated termination of an exited process may fail with access denied.
Job termination applies to associated processes and nested children, with behavior as individual process termination.
PID identity may be reused after process handles close and the object is freed; retain-handle waiting and creation identity diagnostics serve different roles.
